newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended virtually unchanged on Tuesday, erasing all initial gains after new U.S. data offered arguments in favour of a possible Fed tightening on March 25, dealers said.
"After U.S. revised Q4 non-farm unitary labour costs to 2.5 percent from 1.4, the market changed its mind, and treasuries were falling," said Valentin Fernandez at Credit Lyonnais.

He said Bonos were better supported than the Italian market because of positive expectations of a favourable February CPI rate, due on Thursday, which is expected to fall to 2.7/2.8 percent year-on-year from the previous 2.9 percent.
"But Spain's market is confused - it can be supported by good domestic news, but it's also scared by new remarks over EMU," a dealer in Madrid added.
Spain's yield curve steepened in anticipation of tame CPI, with the two to 10-year differential at 125 bps from 121 bps this morning.
On Wednesday, the Spanish Treasury will offer six-month bills, whose yields are expected to be in line or a bit lower in comparison with the two-week-ago auction, dealers said.
